lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: sample spaces, unions, intersections, and complements
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: sample spaces, unions, intersections, and complements

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Group X: 12 successes, 8 failures. Find P(success | X).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: Two events have P(A) = 8/10, P(B) = 3/10, and P(A and B) = 24/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.

items.prompt: In a group of 62, 41 do activity A, 26 do activity B, and 18 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An event has probability 2/4 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 42 successes and 28 failures; group Y with 48 successes and 36 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 3/10, P(B) = 8/10, and P(A and B) = 28/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 41, 26 do activity A, 21 do activity B, and 10 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: An event has probability 2/5 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A survey table records: group X with 37 successes and 32 failures; group Y with 40 successes and 39 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
